I built a free browser tool for drafting invoice reminder emails

Following up on an invoice can be awkward, so I built NudgePay. Enter the invoice details once, then compare 15 English drafts across five timing stages and three tones: polite, standard, and firm. You can copy a draft or open it in your email app to review and send yourself. The tool has no signup and does not send emails or track payments.

Try it: app/

If you freelance, which timing stage or tone would you change first?

posts.text:
I built NudgePay to make invoice follow-ups less awkward — feedback welcome

I built a small tool around one question: is it more useful to compare timing and tone than to start from a single reminder template? NudgePay fills 15 written English templates across five timing stages and three tones. It suggests send dates, but you review the draft and send it yourself. The browser tool is free and requires no account.

Try it: app/

For anyone who invoices clients: which part would you change first, the timing choices, the tone options, or the wording?

Show HN: NudgePay – invoice reminder drafts for freelancers
app/

I built a browser tool that fills 15 written reminder templates for one invoice: five timing stages and three tones. You can copy a draft or open it in your email app; the tool does not send or schedule messages. It requires no signup and saves invoice entries in the browser. I would appreciate feedback on the timing suggestions and wording.
